name: Harsja
title: Levite and father of Ussi
summary: Harsja was a Levite mentioned in the genealogies concerning Israel's return from exile in Babylon. He is known as part of the Levitical lineage that served in the temple after its rebuilding. He is mentioned in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah as part of the restoration of the Jewish community.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Levitical genealogy
keyEvents.description: Harsja is mentioned as part of the Levitical lineage that returned from the Babylonian exile and served in the temple in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: The service of the Levites in the rebuilt temple
keyEvents.description: As part of the Levitical family, Harsja's descendants contributed to the service in the restored temple in Jerusalem after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Recording of genealogies
keyEvents.description: Harsja's name was recorded among the Levitical families as part of the careful keeping of lineages after the return from Babylon.

keyEvents.title: The role of the Levites in renewing the covenant
keyEvents.description: The Levites, including descendants of the family of Harsha, participated in renewing the covenant with God under the leadership of Ezra and Nehemiah.
